chapter: French Quarter music, then and now
title: Music in the French Quarter in recent summers
summary: Wood describes the gazebo, Cafe Mediterranean and tent bands, Olympia Brass, the Junior Olympia band, and the Cafe Mediterranean group he finds too touristy.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh, good. Well, these last few summers, you say five summers, you've been here.
Have you gone to, Decatur Street, from the beginning?

Just sort of, wandered by, and to the, to the gazebo, and to the, Cafe Mediterranean, you know, I usually wander over there, and listen to what's going on, after I've heard, whatever's at the tent, and sometimes, the music is really, pretty good. Sometimes, I don't like it much. It depends, maybe on, my mood, and maybe how many beers, I've had, by the afternoon, and where it's on, but, then at the gazebo, some of that music, is pretty good. I've enjoyed, John Royan's piano playing, right much down there, and, I don't know, what is it, that, the fellow's name, that plays the clarinet down there, who's an Englishman, been around for a while. Chris Burke. Chris Burke, wears his hair, kind of in a bang,
in the front. That's him, yeah. No, no, I just wondered, how that compared, with the music, of years gone by, if any of the bands, down there, sound like the old-timey band.
At the gazebo? Yeah. Or, Cafe Mediterranean. Or the tent. Yeah,

the tent bands, sometimes do. They don't sound like, well, I guess, the only band, that I've heard down there, that really builds itself, as a brass band, was, three weeks ago, this summer, I think it was, the Onward Brass Band,
Dijans, oh, the Olympia, not the Onward, the Olympia Brass.

I don't really enjoy them, particularly, although I was kind of interested, they had, the Junior Olympia Brass Band, and all these little kids, and it was kind of fun, to see those little kids play. Some guy, a little bitty guy, must have been, no more than nine, ten years old, really get a lot of sound, out of the trumpet. But then, a couple, weeks later, walking down Bourbon Street, they were up, playing it on the street, and passing the hat, the, you know, but, you know, that setting, that concert setting, is, is really not the same, ambience, as, as the whole thing was. I have enjoyed, very much, hearing, some of those concerts, down in the, in the, at the tent, in the French Quarter. Last summer, I remember hearing, Chester's artists play, that was, just a wonderful, musical afternoon, down there. and then, the group that was there, last, Sunday. But that, you know, that's an orchestra, not a brass band.

But, I love the music, and I, I like the, the, really, I like the traditional, music, um, over at the Café Mediterranean, that is just a little too hokey for me, that's too, too, too tourist, uh, oriented, somehow, or all. I just don't really.
